correctness.rationale: For 0<β<1, g±=y±aβ(y), aβ=y(1−y)(y−β), derivatives |aβ′|<1 on [0,1], so increasing homeomorphisms fix and preserve 0,β,1 and invariant open strips. Fair signs make each Y_n(y) a bounded martingale. Conditional quadratic variation ∑E aβ(Y_n(y))²<∞ forces limiting zeros of aβ, and expectation gives endpoint selection probabilities y/β below β and (y−β)/(1−β) above. Coupled monotonicity and a countable rational-dense argument produce simultaneous separating thresholds for all other starting heights, giving exact uniform marginal CDFs. Conditional product drift E[X_{n+1}Z_{n+1}−X_nZ_n | past]=aβ(X_n)aβ(Z_n)<0. Cauchy–Schwarz on quadratic variation ensures absolute convergence of its telescoping series; atomless cuts identify limit joint event, proving strict negative quadrant dependence and covariance. Independently checked the exact β=1/2, u=1/4, v=3/4 first-term bound 247/1024 by rational arithmetic.

value.rationale: The cubic skew product is a motivated canonical intermingled-basin example. Uniform marginals provide exact expected sizes of all three basins, while strictly negative dependence disproves naive independence of basin boundaries and gives a quantitative exact signed error series. These are natural dynamical observables rather than an arbitrary numeric plot.
residual_risks: The findings depend on fair independent driving and identical parameter β; not asserted for biased or asymmetric maps.
